title: Proactive degradation: regional bleed-gate and soft-quarantine controller
author: Leah Kim
description:
Motivation: we observed two incidents where a single noisy tenant in one region caused aggressive circuit tripping that then cascaded to neighboring regions during the repair window. The existing SLO enforcer was binary (open/closed) and the region eviction logic had no controlled leak to let limited best-effort traffic continue to high-priority routes. This PR introduces a "bleed-gate" controller and a soft-quarantine mode to allow graded SLO concessions and safe, time-bound traffic leaking during partial outages.

What this changes: adds a controller that: (1) monitors per-tenant and per-route SLO burn-rate across a region boundary, (2) when SLO pressure is sustained, transitions the tenant/route into soft-quarantine where traffic is rate-limited by a graded token allotment rather than fully evicted, (3) exports hysteresis-aware metrics to avoid flapping and (4) integrates an emergency override that the control plane can flip for manual recovery. The bleed-gate implements a token-decay model that allows a configurable fraction of requests to pass (e.g., 5-20%) with priority-preserving admission to reduce global outage impact while preserving fastest warm-path for high-value requests.

Design notes: the bleed-gate is implemented as a separate controller (regional_quarantine_controller) that subscribes to the SLO enforcer's decision events and to the serving runtime's health telemetry. It maintains ephemeral state in memory with a bounded snapshot persisted to the runtime state-store every 10s to survive controller restarts. Hysteresis uses a two-window approach: a short window (30s) for surge detection and a longer window (5m) for stability before escalation. Soft-quarantine levels are configured per-customer class via config/defaults.yaml and exposed in the Console as an opt-in experimental feature.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.bleed_gate; default disabled. Step 1: enable for internal canary tenants in us-west-2 (1 day), observe metrics and error budgets for 24h. Step 2: expand to beta customers in two regions (3 days) with telemetry retention 7d. Step 3: GA if no regression to error budgets or latency SLOs. Automatic rollback path implemented via circuit-breaker: controller flips to full-eviction if soft-quarantine fails to reduce SLO burn by 30% after 10m.

Testing and safety: unit tests for the token-decay math, integration tests simulating cross-region traffic spikes, and an e2e smoke harness that validates no single-tenancy can cause global degradation when soft-quarantine engages. CI adds a new integration job that runs the controller in a lightweight k8s test environment with injected latency.

Migration & compat: config/defaults.yaml adds safe defaults. No customer-visible API changes to the Redwood REST endpoints; behavior is behind feature-flag and console toggle.

Related work: ENG-1782 (SLO enforcer refactor), ENG-2105 (regional telemetry standardization), PM-342 (Console feature flags).

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation
- [x] Token-decay admission algorithm with unit tests
- [x] Integration and e2e smoke tests
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards (prometheus metrics + Console graphs)
- [x] Feature flag and rollout plan
- [x] Documentation update (API docs + runbook)

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the initial admission conservative (low bleed percentage) and provides a manual override in the Console for incident responders. Observability includes a new prometheus metric bleed_gate_level{region,tenant,route} and an alert rule that fires if bleed_gate_level > 0 for >15m with no subsequent SLO budget improvement.

review_conversation: Aisha Patel (reviewer): The token-decay math looks sound but add a comment explaining the choice of the 0.3 decay constant. Also, can we expose a debug endpoint for snapshots?

Leah Kim (author): Added comment and a debug-only HTTP handler behind feature flag in serving/controller/bleed_gate.go. The decay constant was chosen after load testing; documented rationale in docs/runbooks/bleed_gate.md
Marco Liu (reviewer): Observability: can you add a histogram for admitted request latency when bleed gate is active so we can ensure tail latencies don't regress?
Leah Kim (author): Added bleed_gate_admit_latency histogram and Console graph wiring. Integration tests assert no tail latency regression above 95th percentile for admission path.
Bradley O'Neal (reviewer): Small nits: prefer ctx-aware shutdown and better error wrapping in state_store snapshot flush. Also, there's a potential race on startup observed locally.

Leah Kim (author): Addressed ctx shutdown and error wrapping. Added a short-delay retry on startup snapshot restore to mitigate controller ordering with state-store; added hotfix-0 commit to the PR to fix race. Re-ran integration tests.
Aisha Patel (approver): Approving once integration passes and we have a follow-up to expose per-tenant opt-out via Console (PM had asked).
release_notes: Introduces experimental regional bleed-gate and soft-quarantine controller (feature-flagged). Default off. Provides graded admission to reduce cross-region cascade risk; includes telemetry and runbook. Opt-in for canary and beta customers.
